sources.title: Three-dimensional tuning of idiophone bar modes via finite element analysis
sources.role: Yamaha C4 dimensions and minimum undercut thickness, aluminium material values, and the approximately 1:4:10 target for the first three vertical-flexural modes

sources.role: one-dimensional beam finite elements with simplified rectangular undercut height and length design variables

sources.title: Vibraphone, J.C. Deagan, Model 145
sources.role: corroborating 37-bar manufacturing envelope only; not a per-key measurement authority

sources.title: Aluminum 6061-T6 (UNS AA96061)
sources.role: published 4 K to 300 K curve-fit coefficients for thermal conductivity, specific heat, Young modulus, and linear expansion; evaluated at the authority-owned temperature for thermoelastic damping only

sources.title: Thermoelastic damping in micro- and nanomechanical systems
sources.role: primary exact thin-beam thermoelastic loss law; Eq. 29 replaces the single-relaxation Zener approximation as the generated loss component

acoustics.convention: Exact offline resonator and compact-radiation design constants for dry air at 20 C; not a weather-dependent runtime atmosphere model.

perKeyDesignLaw.claim: C4 is measured; other keys are deterministic physical designs inside the corroborating envelope, not measured per-key replicas

measuredC4MonotonicLengthPolicy.law: The measured C4 length is a hard monotonic anchor: lower-pitched designs cannot be shorter and higher-pitched designs cannot be longer.

hierarchy.law: Every key must admit f1 and f2/f1 approximately 4. MIDI 53 and the measured Yamaha C4 at MIDI 60 must additionally admit f3/f1 approximately 10; other keys retain f3 as a causal prediction only when that third target is infeasible.

thermoelasticBeam.steppedBeamComposition: For every mode n, eta_TED[n]=sum_e strainEnergyFraction[n,e]*eta_exact(omega_n,h_e); fractions are nonnegative and sum to one.
thermoelasticBeam.structuralYoungModulusPolicy: The beam solve retains the Beaton-Scavone 68.9 GPa design datum. The independently evaluated NIST modulus is used inside Delta only; the two authorities are not silently conflated.

support.fieldInterpolation: cubic-Hermite element field from M-normalized displacement and rotation DOFs

radiation.modeIntegralQuadrature: four-point Gauss-Legendre per stepped beam element over the cubic-Hermite M-normalized displacement field
radiation.dipoleSeparationH: outerThicknessM, the top-to-bottom separation of the uncut bar envelope
radiation.law: R_ac=rho_air*omega^2/(4*pi*c); c_mode=R_ac*4*sin(k*h/2)^2*(width*integral(phi dx))^2; eta_radiation=c_mode/omega. The finite-separation factor is bounded and tends to (k*h)^2 at low k*h.

damper.law: When engaged at runtime, c_mode=c_damper*phi(x_contact)^2 and is added to the free-decay modal damping; it is never baked into generated free T60 values.

noClaim: Only the Yamaha C4 geometry is a measured per-key design anchor.
The one-dimensional solver does not identify lateral or torsional three-dimensional modes.
The fourth and higher flexural frequencies are predictions, not reviewed tuning targets.
Geometry causality and eigen residuals do not establish corpus similarity or listening acceptance.
The composite free-decay model is not a measured per-key T60 identification; its support coefficient and compact radiation approximation require independent acoustic validation.
The runtime damper coefficient is a declared contact-model design parameter and is excluded from the generated free-decay T60 values.
The exact Lifshitz-Roukes thermoelastic component is still orders too weak to identify seconds-scale vibraphone decay by itself; no total-T60 claim is inferred from it.
